The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Ashok Kumar Samle on 6
March, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:18253

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice B. P. Sharma

On The 6 th Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 1094 of 2015
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Versus
 Ashok Kumar Samle
 Appearance:
 Chhoti Kushram - Advocate for the respondent [R-1].
 Order

Being aggrieved by the judgment of acquittal dated 04.02.2014 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Hoshangabad District Hoshangabad (MP) in Criminal Case No.1473/2011 whereby the trial court has acquitted the respondent from the offences punishable U/s 2(ia), 7((i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Adhiniyam, 1954, the petitioner/State has filed this petition seeking to leave to appeal.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Hoshangabad District Hoshangabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the record and impugned judgment.
3.
Rule 14 of the Act, 1954 mandates that Food Inspector collects samples in clean and dry bottles.
Rule 14 is mandatory and failure to comply with it will render the prosecution against the accused tainted.
In the case at hand, Food Inspector Shivraj Pawak (PW-1) collected the milk sample in clean, colourless, odourless and clean bottles after mixing it with formalin preservative.

However,
Rule 14 has not been followed and samples have not NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18253 2 MCRC-1094-2015 be collected in clean and dry bottles.
This Rule has clearly not been complied by the Food Inspector at the time of taking samples.
Therefore, in this case prosecution case is found to be tainted based on the legal position.
4. It is further mentioned here that Rules 17 and 18 of Act is also mandatory.
In this case, Rule 17 and 18 was not followed by the prosecution.

From the perusal of oral and documentary evidence presented by the prosecution, it is seen that in the complaint filed by the Food Inspector, Shivraj Pawak and the statement given by him, he has not stated that sample was separately sealed in dry bottles and sent it to the State Food Testing Laboratory, Bhopal.

In such circumstances, it appears that the prosecution did not comply with the mandatory Rules 14, 17 and 18 of Act and due to The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Ashok Kumar Samle on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160900716/
1 non-compliance of the mandatory rules, the trial court has rightly acquitted the respondent.
5. On perusal of the impugned order, the trial Court has duly considered the entire evidence adduced by the prosecution as well as the legal position as mentioned in the impugned judgment and the trial court has rightly given the benefit of doubt and acquitted the respondent/accused.
6.
